docs.name: alex-rivera-resume.pdf
docs.text:
Alex Rivera, Staff Product Designer. Ten years designing and shipping interfaces for data-heavy products, most recently leading design for an AI research assistant used by analysts at large financial firms. I work across research, interaction design, prototyping and front-end code, and I care most about turning ambiguous model behavior into interfaces people can trust.

Experience, Northwind Analytics, Staff Product Designer, 2021 to now. Led the redesign of the assistant workspace from a single chat column into a document-centered layout with citations, side-by-side sources and saved threads. Partnered with research to run weekly sessions with analysts, which reshaped the citation model twice. Built the first production prototype of streaming answers in React and TypeScript and worked with engineering to ship it to forty thousand seats. Introduced an evaluation review where designers score real model transcripts each sprint, which cut reported trust issues by a third over two quarters. Mentored four designers and ran the design critique for the AI group.

Experience, Lumen Health, Senior Product Designer, 2017 to 2021. Owned the clinician scheduling and messaging surfaces across web and iOS. Designed the shared component library used by three product teams, including accessible form controls, tables and an alerting system that met WCAG 2.1 AA. Led the move from static mockups to coded prototypes for every major feature, so usability tests ran against real data. Worked closely with compliance on consent and privacy flows, and wrote the content guidelines for error and empty states that the whole product adopted.

Experience, Fieldnote, Product Designer, 2014 to 2017. Early designer at a note-taking startup that grew from beta to two hundred thousand users. Designed onboarding, sync conflict handling and the first collaborative editing features. Wrote production CSS and small React components alongside the front-end team, and set up the visual regression checks the team still uses. Ran the first pricing experiments and the redesign of the upgrade flow, which doubled trial conversion.

Skills and tools. Interaction and visual design, design systems, prototyping in code, React, TypeScript, CSS, Figma, user research, usability testing, evaluation of language model output, prompt design, accessibility, motion design. Education, BFA in Interaction Design, California College of the Arts. Speaking, talks on designing for model uncertainty at two design conferences, and a workshop on writing evaluation rubrics with product teams.

Selected projects. A citation viewer that lets readers jump from any claim to the exact passage it came from, with highlights that survive document edits. A comparison mode for two reports that lines up matching sections and flags disagreements. A guided setup for teams connecting their own documents, with clear explanations of what is stored, for how long, and who can see it. A small internal tool that turns usability notes into tagged findings so patterns show up across studies.

Earlier work and community. Before Fieldnote I freelanced for two years, designing marketing sites and small web apps for local nonprofits, a public library system and a regional transit agency. That work taught me to explain design decisions to people who are not designers, to write plain interface copy, and to ship within tight budgets. I still volunteer as a mentor in a design apprenticeship program, reviewing portfolios and running mock interviews each quarter. I also maintain a small open source library of accessible React form patterns that a few hundred teams use, and I write occasional essays about designing interfaces for uncertain systems, including how to show confidence, sources and limits without overwhelming the reader.

What I am looking for. A team building tools that people rely on for real decisions, where design sits close to research and engineering and has a say in how models are evaluated. I want to own a product area end to end, from early research and prototypes through launch and iteration, and to keep writing code in the interface layer. I am most excited about agent interfaces, document understanding, and making it easy for people to check an answer against its sources. I prefer hybrid work in the Bay Area, and I am open to staff or principal level roles with mentoring responsibilities.
